newsitem.title: BURMA: Burmese students stage sit-in protest on campus.
newsitem.headline: Burmese students stage sit-in protest on campus.

text.p: About 100 students at the Yangon Institute of Technology (YIT) on Monday staged a peaceful sit-in inside the campus to show their displeasure at leaflets urging them to improve their behaviour, witnesses said.
The protest was also related to police handling of a brawl in October between students and restaurant owners that led to a rare street demonstration by about 500 university students.
The students, who gathered inside the institute's main hall, did not heed a request by instructors to return to class. By mid-afternoon on Monday they had still refused to disperse.
"The students are still inside," said one YIT official. "We are trying to control the situation peacefully. We are expecting the minister (of education) to come to talk to them."
Sources near YIT, which is off-limits to anyone but students or faculty members, said the protesting students did not move outside campus walls and police had not intervened.

Witnesses said the protesting students were upset about leaflets, apparently distributed by another group of students, urging their classmates not to get involved in activities that could disrupt their studies.

They were also unhappy about the way police handled the October brawl, which resulted in the brief arrest of three students. The October demonstration was to protest at the rough handling of the students by police while under arrest.
Officials later detained Kyi Maung, deputy chairman of the National League for Democracy (NLD) party, for questioning for about a week to determine his role in the protests.
The day before the October demonstration, two students were seen speaking with Kyi Maung for about an hour at the home of democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi.
The protesting YIT students on Monday demanded that two students who were requested not to attend classes after the October brawl be allowed to return to their studies.
The students also demanded that authorities clarify within 24 hours whether any action had been taken against police responsible for the arrests of their colleagues in October.
They also sought a promise that the YIT would not be closed because of the latest protest on Monday, YIT sources said.
Although the school was not closed after the October demonstration, it was shut for about two years following nationwide pro-democracy uprisings in 1988.

The 1988 student-led demonstrations, which were quashed by the State Law and Order Restoration Council with thousands killed or imprisoned, were sparked by a teashop brawl that incited nationwide outrage against the military government.
